quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the weather stays clear this weekend, we'll drive up to the lake.
quests.sentence: ____ the weather stays clear this weekend, we'll drive up to the lake.
quests.hint: Going to the lake depends on something that might or might not happen - this isn't a certainty.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces a condition - the trip depends on the weather, which isn't guaranteed. 'When' would suggest the clear weather is a sure thing, which isn't what this sentence means.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ you need any help setting up the new system, just call the IT desk.
quests.sentence: ____ you need any help setting up the new system, just call the IT desk.
quests.hint: This offers help only in case a certain situation comes up - it's not guaranteed to happen.
quests.explanation: 'If' sets up a possible situation - needing help - that may or may not occur. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest a reason rather than a condition.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ you leave milk out of the fridge for too long, it goes bad quickly.
quests.sentence: ____ you leave milk out of the fridge for too long, it goes bad quickly.
quests.hint: This describes a general rule that's true whenever the condition is met, not one specific event.
quests.explanation: 'If' works well here to state a general conditional truth. 'Because' would only work if we were explaining why milk had already gone bad in one specific instance.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ your package hasn't arrived within five business days, please contact our support team.
quests.sentence: ____ your package hasn't arrived within five business days, please contact our support team.
quests.hint: This describes a possible problem that may or may not occur - not a certainty.
quests.explanation: 'If' sets up the possible situation of a late package. 'When' would incorrectly suggest the delay is guaranteed to happen.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ you don't understand a question on the test, skip it and come back later.
quests.sentence: ____ you don't understand a question on the test, skip it and come back later.
quests.hint: Not understanding a question is just a possibility, not something guaranteed for every student.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces this possible scenario. 'When' would suggest every student is certain to face a confusing question, which overstates things.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ you feel any sharp pain during the exercise, stop immediately and rest.
quests.sentence: ____ you feel any sharp pain during the exercise, stop immediately and rest.
quests.hint: Feeling pain is a possible warning sign, not something expected to happen to everyone.
quests.explanation: 'If' sets up this possible situation as a safety instruction. 'Because' would incorrectly frame it as an explanation rather than a condition to watch for.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the meeting runs late, we'll just reschedule the lunch for another day.
quests.sentence: ____ the meeting runs late, we'll just reschedule the lunch for another day.
quests.hint: Running late is only a possibility here, not something we know for sure will happen.
quests.explanation: 'If' captures the uncertainty about whether the meeting will run late. 'When' would incorrectly suggest it's already expected to run late.
quests.grammarRule: Condition vs Time - if (uncertain), not when (certain)

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the school bell rings at 3pm, students are dismissed for the day.
quests.sentence: ____ the school bell rings at 3pm, students are dismissed for the day.
quests.hint: The bell ringing at 3pm happens every single day without fail - this isn't uncertain at all.
quests.explanation: 'When' fits because the bell ringing is a certain, routine event, not a possibility. 'If' would incorrectly suggest there's doubt about whether the bell will ring.
quests.grammarRule: Time vs Condition - when (certain), not if (uncertain)

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ grandma visits this weekend, we should plan a special dinner - though she hasn't confirmed yet.
quests.sentence: ____ grandma visits this weekend, we should plan a special dinner - though she hasn't confirmed yet.
quests.hint: The phrase 'hasn't confirmed yet' tells you this isn't a sure thing.
quests.explanation: 'If' matches the uncertainty explicitly mentioned - her visit isn't confirmed. 'When' would wrongly suggest the visit is already a certainty.
quests.grammarRule: Condition vs Time - if, not when

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ you book your tickets soon, the prices will keep going up.
quests.sentence: ____ you book your tickets soon, the prices will keep going up.
quests.hint: This means the same as 'if you don't book soon' - look for the connector that already builds in that 'not.'
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not,' so it already includes the negative idea without needing an extra 'not' in the sentence. 'If' would need an added 'don't' to express the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ you submit the form by Friday, your application won't be considered this round.
quests.sentence: ____ you submit the form by Friday, your application won't be considered this round.
quests.hint: This means 'if you don't submit by Friday' - the connector already builds that 'not' in for you.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if...not,' so the sentence doesn't need an extra negative. Using 'if' here would require rewriting the sentence with 'don't submit' to keep the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ everyone finishes their chores, there will be no dessert tonight.
quests.sentence: ____ everyone finishes their chores, there will be no dessert tonight.
quests.hint: This warns of a consequence that happens only if the chores are NOT finished.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' captures this built-in negative condition - no dessert unless chores are done. 'If' would need to be rephrased with 'don't finish' to carry the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the printer has enough toner left, we can finish printing all the handouts before the meeting.
quests.sentence: ____ the printer has enough toner left, we can finish printing all the handouts before the meeting.
quests.hint: This describes a possibility that may or may not be true - finishing the handouts depends on whether there's enough toner.
quests.explanation: 'If' correctly introduces the condition of having enough toner. 'Unless' would reverse the meaning, suggesting printing only happens when there ISN'T enough toner.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ both parties sign the agreement, the deal cannot move forward.
quests.sentence: ____ both parties sign the agreement, the deal cannot move forward.
quests.hint: The deal is stuck only in the case where signing does NOT happen - look for the connector that already carries that built-in 'not.'
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means the deal can't proceed without both signatures. 'If' would need 'don't sign' added to express the same meaning, since the sentence as written has no separate negative.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ you cancel within 24 hours, you'll be charged the full appointment fee.
quests.sentence: ____ you cancel within 24 hours, you'll be charged the full appointment fee.
quests.hint: The fee applies specifically when cancellation does NOT happen in time - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the fee applies unless you cancel in time. 'If' would need to be rewritten with 'don't cancel' to carry the same meaning as written.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ you miss three loan payments in a row, the bank can repossess the car.
quests.sentence: ____ you miss three loan payments in a row, the bank can repossess the car.
quests.hint: This describes a possible future scenario and its consequence, not something that has already happened.
quests.explanation: 'If' sets up a hypothetical situation with a clear consequence. 'Because' would only fit if we were explaining why a car had already been repossessed.
quests.grammarRule: Condition vs Reason - if, not because

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The project was delayed ____ two key team members were out sick for a week.
quests.sentence: The project was delayed ____ two key team members were out sick for a week.
quests.hint: This is explaining something that already happened, not describing a possible future situation.
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains the actual reason for a delay that already occurred. 'If' would incorrectly turn this into a hypothetical situation, which doesn't match the completed, factual event being described.
quests.grammarRule: Reason vs Condition - because, not if

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: Grace won't let her son watch TV tonight ____ he hasn't finished his homework yet.
quests.sentence: Grace won't let her son watch TV tonight ____ he hasn't finished his homework yet.
quests.hint: This explains the actual, current reason for her decision - not a hypothetical possibility.
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains the real, current reason behind her decision. 'If' would incorrectly frame the unfinished homework as merely a possible future situation, when it's already true right now.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the recipe called for fresh basil, Tom used dried basil instead and it still tasted great.
quests.sentence: ____ the recipe called for fresh basil, Tom used dried basil instead and it still tasted great.
quests.hint: Using a substitute ingredient and still getting a great result despite the recipe's instructions is the unexpected twist here.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the recipe's requirement and Tom's substitution still working out well. 'If' would incorrectly turn this into a hypothetical rather than something that actually happened.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the refund is processed, you'll receive a confirmation email.
quests.sentence: ____ the refund is processed, you'll receive a confirmation email.
quests.hint: There's essentially no gap between the refund being processed and the email arriving.
quests.explanation: 'As soon as' emphasizes the immediate sequence between the refund and the confirmation. 'If' would incorrectly suggest the refund itself is uncertain, when the sentence is really about timing.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: Your subscription will renew automatically at full price ____ you cancel before the trial period ends.
quests.sentence: Your subscription will renew automatically at full price ____ you cancel before the trial period ends.
quests.hint: The automatic renewal happens only in the case where cancellation does NOT occur in time.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the renewal happens specifically when cancellation doesn't occur. 'If' would need 'don't cancel' added to express the same idea.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ you wear proper safety goggles, you won't be allowed on the construction site.
quests.sentence: ____ you wear proper safety goggles, you won't be allowed on the construction site.
quests.hint: Being kept off site happens specifically when goggles are NOT worn - which connector already carries that built-in 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows entry is blocked when goggles aren't worn. 'If' would need 'don't wear' added to express the same restriction.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ your passport is valid for at least six months, you won't be permitted to board the flight.
quests.sentence: ____ your passport is valid for at least six months, you won't be permitted to board the flight.
quests.hint: Boarding is blocked in the specific case where the passport does NOT meet that requirement.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' captures this built-in negative condition about passport validity. 'If' would require rewording with 'isn't valid' to mean the same thing.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The gym will freeze your membership fee ____ you provide a doctor's note explaining the injury.
quests.sentence: The gym will freeze your membership fee ____ you provide a doctor's note explaining the injury.
quests.hint: The freeze happens specifically when the note IS provided - not when it's missing.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces this straightforward positive condition. 'Unless' would reverse the meaning, suggesting the freeze happens only when the note is NOT provided.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The courier will leave the package at your door ____ someone signs for it in person.
quests.sentence: The courier will leave the package at your door ____ someone signs for it in person.
quests.hint: Leaving it at the door happens specifically when no one is there to sign - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the package is left at the door only when no one signs for it. 'If' would need 'doesn't sign' added to carry the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ your claim includes all the required documents, processing usually takes about two weeks.
quests.sentence: ____ your claim includes all the required documents, processing usually takes about two weeks.
quests.hint: This describes what happens on the condition that something is true, not an explanation of something that has already occurred.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces the condition about the claim being complete. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation of a specific past outcome rather than a general condition.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The kids can watch one more episode ____ it's already past their bedtime.
quests.sentence: The kids can watch one more episode ____ it's already past their bedtime.
quests.hint: The permission depends on it NOT already being past bedtime - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the episode is off-limits specifically when it's already past bedtime. 'If' would need 'isn't' added to express the same restriction.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the contractor finishes the roof repairs before storm season begins, the insurance company will waive the increased premium.
quests.sentence: ____ the contractor finishes the roof repairs before storm season begins, the insurance company will waive the increased premium.
quests.hint: The waived premium depends on the repairs actually being finished in time, not on them being missed.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces this positive condition clearly. 'Unless' would reverse the logic, suggesting the premium is waived only when the repairs are NOT finished.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The community center will lose its funding next year ____ attendance numbers improve significantly over the next few months.
quests.sentence: The community center will lose its funding next year ____ attendance numbers improve significantly over the next few months.
quests.hint: Losing funding happens specifically if attendance does NOT improve - which connector already carries that built-in 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the funding loss depends on attendance failing to improve. 'If' would need 'doesn't improve' added to express the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The volunteer coordinator canceled Saturday's event ____ fewer than five people had signed up by the deadline.
quests.sentence: The volunteer coordinator canceled Saturday's event ____ fewer than five people had signed up by the deadline.
quests.hint: This explains the actual reason the event was canceled, not a hypothetical future condition.
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains the real reason behind the cancellation, which already happened. 'If' or 'unless' would incorrectly frame this as a hypothetical situation rather than something that occurred.
